questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: In a story, Jess walks along the sand at Bondi Beach as the waves crash. What is the setting of this part of the story?
questions.explanation: The setting is where the story happens. Here it is Bondi Beach.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: In a story, Ben shares his lunch with a new boy who sits alone. What does this show about Ben?
questions.explanation: Sharing food with someone who is alone shows Ben is kind.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: In a story, a koala loses her way. Then she meets a wombat. The wombat shows her the path home. What is the problem in this story?
questions.explanation: The problem is the trouble the character has. The koala is lost.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: A story has these events. Sam packs a bag. Sam walks to the bus stop. Sam waves goodbye at school camp. Which event happens last?
choices: Sam walks to the bus stop
Sam waves goodbye at school camp
questions.explanation: The events are in order, so the last one written happens last. Sam waves goodbye at camp.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: An author writes: "Her eyes grew wide and her hands began to shake." How does the girl feel?
questions.explanation: Wide eyes and shaking hands are signs of being frightened.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: An author writes: "The old shed leaned to one side. Its tin roof was full of rusty holes." What does this tell us about the shed?
questions.explanation: Leaning walls and rusty holes show the shed is old and falling apart.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: An author writes: "Mr Dale was as grumpy as a wet cat." What is the author telling us about Mr Dale?
choices: He is wet from the rain
questions.explanation: The author compares Mr Dale to a wet cat to show he is grumpy.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: An author can show a character is shy by describing how the character acts.
questions.explanation: Actions, like hiding behind a parent, can show a character is shy.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Onomatopoeia is a word that sounds like the noise it names. Which word is onomatopoeia in this sentence? "The sausages sizzled on the barbecue."
questions.explanation: The word sizzled sounds like the noise sausages make when they cook.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: What do we call the beat that you can hear when you read a poem aloud?
questions.explanation: Rhythm is the beat of the words. Rhyme is when words end with the same sound.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: An author writes: "The drum went boom, boom, boom." Why does the author use the word boom?
choices: To make the reader hear the sound
To say where the story happens
questions.explanation: Boom sounds like a drum, so the reader can almost hear it.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: A poem says: "Run, run, jump, hop!" The words are short and quick. How does this make the poem feel?
questions.explanation: Short, quick words give the poem a fast rhythm that feels lively.
